memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made two gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod. Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the shoulder-pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above the waistband of the ephod. They tied the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with blue cord, connecting it to the waistband so that the breastpiece would not swing out from the ephod - as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God states the reason plainly: "so that the breastpiece would not swing out from the ephod."

Four rings, blue cord, tied top and bottom. The names over the heart had to stay pressed close, not flapping about as the priest moved.

Think about what that pictures. God's people are not held at arm's length, dangling. They are bound tight against the priest's chest.

Jesus prayed that we would be with Him where He is (John 17:24). Paul says we have been raised with Christ and our life is now hidden with Him in God (Col 3:3). Hidden — tucked in close, not held out at a distance.

There is also a word here about our own closeness to God. Cords had to be deliberately tied. Left alone, the breastpiece would have swung away. Left alone, our hearts drift too.

James gives the remedy simply: come near to God and He will come near to you (Jas 4:8). Jesus said, remain in me, as I also remain in you (John 15:4).

What are the blue cords in your life — the deliberate ties that keep you close when everything else pulls you away?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your life is pulling you away from closeness with God?
2. What deliberate practices keep you tied close to Him?
3. Do you live as someone held close or held at a distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, tie my heart to Yours. Keep me close when everything in my life is pulling me away. Amen.
